#     scripts/verify-proofs.sh --refresh
# and REVIEW THE DIFF: every number below is a claim about how much
# was verified, and the point of committing them is that a drop
# cannot happen without showing up in a merge request.
# Blessed 2026-09-01T13:32:42Z on arm64-Darwin.

# downstream proof consumer cert verify: proof terms replayed from the bundle.
bundle_theorems=414

# compiler_consumer on src/trust_surface.rs: island declarations registered,
# 'by <theorem>' citations kernel-discharged (exact -- losing one is
# silent), and Level-0 obligations, which must ALL be proved.
#
# The obligation total is NOT evidence that the citations are there
# -- not for the 'min' citations.  Measured 2026-08-24: deleting a
# 'by <theorem>' clause from one of those -- the trivial u64_le_refl
# one or the soundness-carrying capcoeff_i64_min_full -- leaves
# compiler_consumer at rc 0 with the total unchanged, because the solver
# re-proves the postcondition unaided.  Only the name and site lists
# below can see such a citation disappear.
#
# The two rule-guard citations behave differently and are worth
# more for it: their clauses come back Unknown from the native
# verifier, so deleting either 'by' drops the total AND fails the
# run on its own.  Do not generalise either behaviour to the other
# group; the lists below are what gates both.
island_decls=912
island_citations=20
island_cited_names=capcoeff_i64_le_capcoeff,capcoeff_i64_le_coeff,capcoeff_i64_le_degree,capcoeff_i64_min_full,capcoeff_le_other,capcoeff_le_self,capcoeff_le_self,capcoeff_min_bounds,checkedAdd128_comm,checkedAdd128_isSome_of_inI64,checkedMul128_comm,checkedMul128_isSome_of_inI64,checkedSub128_isSome_of_inI64,checkedSub128_self_isSome,guard_fits_exact,guard_fits_lower_exact,guard_fits_upper_exact,narrowWide_isSome_of_fits,u64_le_refl,weaken_factor_sign_exact
# '<function>:<theorem>' per citation, as compiler_consumer resolved it ("with
# `result` bound to the imported definition of `<function>`").  The
# name list alone cannot see a citation MIGRATE: 'by
# capcoeff_i64_le_coeff' on a fresh two-line function keeps the name
# list identical while claiming nothing about cap_coeff_i64_le_coeff,
# the function whose body is pinned to the real cap_coeff.

island_proved_obligations=45

# compiler_consumer on the whole crate under the advisory policy.  A RATCHET,
# not a proof: most obligations are open.  Raise the floor and lower
# the ceiling as coverage grows; never the other way round silently.
# 'enabled' runs the ratchet.  Any other value pins the stage
# UNAVAILABLE and inverts the gate (it then REQUIRES the crate-root
# diagnostic, so the crate compiling again is the failure).
#
# It was pinned unavailable while `malachite-bigint` had no build
# step here, and the reason recorded then -- "a dependency compiler_consumer
# cannot build" -- was WRONG.  Measured 2026-08-24: compiler_consumer builds
# malachite-bigint and its whole dependency tree (22 rlibs) in ~9s.
# What was missing was the build step, not the capability: one
# standalone `compiler_consumer src/lib.rs` is E0433 with no --extern, and
# cargo's own rlib is stock-rustc-built, which compiler_consumer refuses with
# E0514.  The script now pre-builds the tree with
# the historical explicit unverified dependency build and
# passes that rlib as --extern, which is what re-enabled this stage.
#
# Verifying the DEPENDENCIES too is a DIFFERENT lane, is not what
# this stage measures, and is still blocked: with verification enabled
# for every crate, `num-traits` ICEs in model-checker-consumer's CHC translator
# ("EQ requires same sort: (_ BitVec 128) and (_ BitVec 64)") and
# `ryu` exceeds the per-function verify budget.  A third blocker
# there -- a SignatureMismatch ICE in the compiler's `dyn` case
# split, tripped by `proc-macro2`'s build script -- was fixed in
# compiler_consumer on 2026-08-24 (see trustc_toolchain below).
wholecrate_ratchet=enabled
wholecrate_proved_floor=128
wholecrate_incomplete_ceiling=447

# The kernel-discharged citations of the WHOLE-CRATE stage, as
# '<function>:<theorem>'.  The two magnitudes above cannot see one
# of these disappear: an audit deleted the `by` from the contracts
# on the REAL cap_coeff and cap_coeff_wide and proved/incomplete
# stayed byte-identical, because the native solver re-proves those
# 'min' postconditions unaided.  This list is what notices -- and
# these are the contracts that sit on the bodies the checker runs,
# so it is the list that most needed to exist.
wholecrate_citation_sites=add_degree_wide:checkedAdd128_isSome_of_inI64,cadd_wide:checkedAdd128_comm,cadd_wide:checkedAdd128_isSome_of_inI64,cap_coeff:capcoeff_i64_min_full,cap_coeff_bounds_u64:capcoeff_min_bounds,cap_coeff_call_site:capcoeff_le_self,cap_coeff_i64:capcoeff_i64_min_full,cap_coeff_i64_le_capcoeff:capcoeff_i64_le_capcoeff,cap_coeff_i64_le_coeff:capcoeff_i64_le_coeff,cap_coeff_i64_le_degree:capcoeff_i64_le_degree,cap_coeff_le_other_u64:capcoeff_le_other,cap_coeff_le_self_u64:capcoeff_le_self,cap_coeff_wide:capcoeff_i128_min_full,cmul_wide:checkedMul128_comm,cmul_wide:checkedMul128_isSome_of_inI64,csub_wide:checkedSub128_isSome_of_inI64,csub_wide:checkedSub128_self_isSome,factor_nonneg:weaken_factor_sign_exact,fits_i64:guard_fits_exact,fits_i64_lower_wide:guard_fits_lower_exact,fits_i64_upper_wide:guard_fits_upper_exact,fits_i64_wide:guard_fits_exact,mul_coeff_wide:checkedMul128_isSome_of_inI64,narrow:narrowWide_isSome_of_fits,narrow_wide_in_range:narrowWide_isSome_of_fits,neg:litctor_var_preserved,negate:litnegate_var_preserved,pos:litctor_var_preserved,sat_term:satterm_coeff_le_degree,saturated_degree:u64_le_refl,sub_degree_wide:checkedSub128_isSome_of_inI64,weaken_factor_nonneg:weaken_factor_sign_exact,wide_at_least:wide_le_exact,wide_nonneg:wide_sign_exact

# Functions compiler_consumer can admit into its proof fragment, ALL of which
# must carry a contract (gate_admissible_coverage). Required by
# require_pins and read at the whole-crate stage, but never written
# here -- so a plain (non---refresh) run aborted with "missing
# pin(s): admissible_functions" and --refresh never healed it.
# Recounted from the SAME E6 sweep the gate reads, so the pin and
# the gate can never disagree about what was measured.
admissible_functions=19

# The verifying toolchains.  Both are per-machine builds with useless
# --version strings, so the revision is the identifier.  A mismatch is
# reported as TOOLCHAIN DRIFT (a failure under --strict): it means the
# numbers above were measured by a different binary.
clean_toolchain=clean 0.2.0|not-a-git-checkout
trustc_toolchain=rustc 1.99.0-dev (compiler_consumer 0.1.0)|v0.8.0-522-g66e9d4fd406
# Machine-specific absolute paths from the historical measurement are omitted.
# The identities above are preserved; AY selects managed tools on PATH and
# does not claim those historical measurements for a current toolchain.

# NOT pinned, deliberately: the .cleancert bytes and the bundle's
# env_hash.  clean export-cert bincodes HashMaps in randomized
# iteration order before zstd, so two exports of byte-identical input
# differ.  Per-theorem type_hash/proof_hash ARE stable, which is why
# the manifest pins those instead.
